questions.stem: In paediatric anaesthesia for imaging, what do purpose-built suites provide for elective lists such as MRI?
questions.answer: Piped gases, induction and recovery areas, integrated monitors, radiology-ready machines

questions.stem: For paediatric elective scans, how are many children commonly sedated?
questions.answer: Under sedation without an anaesthetist

questions.stem: What makes unusual paediatric imaging studies at remote sites riskier?
questions.answer: Poorer kit and staff not used to anaesthetised children

questions.stem: In paediatric imaging anaesthesia, where is oxygen often sourced, and what should be kept as backup?
questions.answer: A cylinder; have a spare

questions.stem: What suction equipment should be dedicated in paediatric imaging anaesthesia?
questions.answer: Anaesthetic suction

questions.stem: What emergency equipment should be present in a paediatric imaging suite?
questions.answer: Resuscitation trolley and defibrillator

questions.stem: In paediatric imaging anaesthesia, where is it usually better to move a child in cardiac arrest?
In paediatric MRI, who should never be let into the MRI room during a child's anaesthetic?
questions.answer: The resuscitation team

questions.stem: For paediatric imaging anaesthesia, which staff are needed, as for any general anaesthetic?
questions.answer: Anaesthetic assistant and recovery nurse

questions.stem: In paediatric imaging, who may help move larger children on and off the table?
questions.answer: Radiology staff

questions.stem: What two requirements apply to anaesthetic equipment used for paediatric imaging?
questions.answer: Meet standards and be familiar to the team

questions.stem: How should children be assessed before paediatric imaging under anaesthesia?
questions.answer: As for any GA, with attention to syndromes and other illnesses

questions.stem: In paediatric imaging anaesthesia, which investigations are common?
In children going for imaging under anaesthesia, which assessment needs particular care?
questions.answer: Airway

questions.stem: With modern shielded, coned X-ray equipment, beyond what distance is exposure negligible?
What personal protection should staff use to minimise radiation exposure during paediatric imaging?
questions.answer: Lead apron, thyroid shield, exposure badge if exposed often

questions.stem: In paediatric imaging, if the child is properly monitored, where should the anaesthetist watch from?
questions.answer: Behind leaded glass

questions.stem: In paediatric imaging, which organs should be shielded where possible?
questions.answer: Testes, ovaries, thyroid and eyes

questions.stem: In paediatric imaging rooms, what can keep anaesthetic kit away from the patient?
questions.answer: Limited space, fixed tables and equipment, dark rooms and many staff

questions.stem: During paediatric imaging, what items snag and dislodge easily?
questions.answer: Long breathing circuits and IV lines

questions.stem: Before paediatric MRI, what should be requested to judge how much slack is needed?
questions.answer: A trial run of the table into the scanner

questions.stem: In paediatric MRI, why are the scanner rooms kept cold?
questions.answer: Superconducting magnets need cooling

questions.stem: In paediatric imaging, for which scans should temperature be measured?
In paediatric MRI, why are warming blankets a concern?
questions.answer: They can degrade images

questions.stem: Which iodinated contrast reactions are dose-dependent?
questions.answer: Heat, pain, vasodilation, cardiac depression, hypotension

questions.stem: Which iodinated contrast reactions are dose-independent?
questions.answer: Nausea and vomiting, hypersensitivity

questions.stem: What percentage of iodinated contrast administrations cause a moderate reaction?
What percentage of iodinated contrast administrations cause a severe reaction?
In iodinated contrast reactions, what does atopy do to the incidence?
What is the mortality rate of iodinated contrast reactions?
For iodinated contrast, which agent type is used for all intra-arterial injections?
In CT imaging, how is a 2D image of a thin cross-section built?
questions.answer: Rotating X-ray source and detector, from many angles

questions.stem: What does CT imaging separate well?
questions.answer: Structures of different density, such as bone and muscle

questions.stem: How long do CT head scans often take?
In CT imaging, what anaesthetic and monitoring equipment can be used?
questions.answer: Any anaesthetic and monitoring equipment

questions.stem: Because CT radiation doses are relatively high, from where should the child be monitored if possible?
questions.answer: The control room

questions.stem: What is the range of patients undergoing paediatric CT?
questions.answer: Well, fasted infants to trauma patients being resuscitated

questions.stem: Airway access is limited for head CT scans, so what should be done first?
questions.answer: Secure the airway before scanning

questions.stem: In paediatric CT, how should IV sites be kept?
questions.answer: Visible and reachable

questions.stem: In paediatric CT, why should metal leads such as ECG cables be kept out of the scan field?
questions.answer: To avoid image artefact

questions.stem: For paediatric CT, moving a child from trolley to table needs ____ for a controlled transfer.
questions.answer: Enough staff

questions.stem: Before paediatric CT with contrast, which allergy must be checked for?
Why is inhalational induction often preferred for elective paediatric CT under anaesthesia?
questions.answer: Many elective cases are infants, where it is often easier than IV

questions.stem: Which airway device is sometimes suitable for a child having a CT scan?
When is an endotracheal tube often better than an LMA for paediatric CT?
questions.answer: Small child with limited access, or chest CT needing brief inspiratory apnoea

questions.stem: What maintenance options are used for paediatric anaesthesia for CT?
questions.answer: Volatile in oxygen with air or nitrous oxide, or propofol infusion

questions.stem: Which induction suits a child with head injury and reduced consciousness going for CT?
How soon can elective paediatric CT patients usually feed and go home?
Where do emergency paediatric CT patients go, depending on the scan and clinical state?
questions.answer: Theatre, ITU or HDU

questions.stem: In MRI, what does radiofrequency energy at the spin frequency do to the spins?
questions.answer: Tips them to 90° to the magnetic field

questions.stem: What property of liquid-helium-cooled wire lets an MRI superconducting magnet carry a huge current?
What is the field strength range, in Tesla, of MRI magnets?
How many Gauss equal one Tesla in MRI field strength?
Roughly how many times stronger is an MRI magnet than Earth's magnetic field?
What is the approximate strength of Earth's magnetic field in Gauss?
questions.answer: 0.3-0.7 Gauss

questions.stem: In MRI, which materials does the magnetic field affect?
questions.answer: Any ferromagnetic material

questions.stem: What does the 0.5 mT (5 Gauss) line mark in an MRI room?
questions.answer: Below 0.5 mT, where the effect is considered minimal

questions.stem: How close to the 0.5 mT line may magnetic material, such as syringe pumps, be kept?
questions.answer: Not closer than the 0.5 mT line

questions.stem: Which labels must anaesthetic equipment carry before use in MRI?
Which MRI equipment label means no risk to patient or staff, but the image may degrade?
What does the label MR compatible mean for equipment used in MRI?
questions.answer: Safe, works normally and does not affect the image

questions.stem: How should MRI monitoring cables be handled to reduce burn risk?
questions.answer: Padded or kept off the skin, never coiled

questions.stem: Which monitoring items are available as MR-compatible for paediatric MRI?
questions.answer: Fibreoptic oximeter cables, temperature probes and carbon fibre ECG electrodes

questions.stem: What effect does long capnography tubing have during MRI?
questions.answer: It delays the reading

questions.stem: Why is the ECG unreliable in an MRI scanner?
questions.answer: Field-induced currents in the heart and great vessels show as artefact

questions.stem: Why might monitor alarms be missed during paediatric MRI?
questions.answer: Over scanner noise, especially with ear defenders

questions.stem: How do many anaesthetists monitor a child during MRI scanning?
questions.answer: Stay outside with a slave monitor, watching through a window

questions.stem: How loud is MRI scanner noise, in decibels?
When should ear defenders go on a child during paediatric MRI?
questions.answer: Once the child is asleep

questions.stem: Which contrast agent is most often used for paediatric MRI?
What happens to ferromagnetic objects in the MRI field?
questions.answer: They accelerate towards the strongest point of the field

questions.stem: What is an MRI quench?
questions.answer: Sudden large release of helium, deliberate or from a fault

questions.stem: Why is an MRI quench dangerous in the scanner room?
questions.answer: Rising helium makes the room hypoxic

questions.stem: What emergencies must the MRI unit be able to manage itself?
questions.answer: CPR, anaphylaxis and anaesthetic complications

questions.stem: What should be watched for in children having paediatric MRI?
questions.answer: Conditions or syndromes with specific anaesthetic concerns

questions.stem: Apart from noise, what else about MRI can be stimulating for a child?
questions.answer: The enclosed space

questions.stem: How are most older, cooperative children scanned in paediatric MRI?
options: Under general anaesthesia with a tube
Heavily sedated with a propofol infusion
Awake, with music and a parent present

questions.stem: Who needs anaesthesia or sedation for paediatric MRI?
questions.answer: Children too young to lie still, or whose condition limits cooperation

questions.stem: What factors guide choosing an ETT or LMA for paediatric MRI?
questions.answer: Age, reflux risk, respiratory function and ICP

questions.stem: When is intermittent positive pressure ventilation needed for a child having MRI?
options: Only for children over ten years
Only when a scan exceeds one hour
Neonates, poor respiratory function or raised ICP

questions.stem: For paediatric MRI maintenance, why might a propofol infusion be chosen?
questions.answer: Easy to titrate, quick offset, may reduce nausea
